questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My master was a double degree offering exchange with this university for my preferred academic track, thus I chose this destination for the topic of education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The administrative team tries to support students with every request and is genuinely kind. However sometimes the academic experience was below expectations for master studies in English.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: We had an incoming guide and for unanswered questions could contact the administrative team.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Welcome meeting for all international students as well as one for my program.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was hard to find something for only a temporary stay. I recommend using Otodom and OLX.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more costly than student housing and in my and my peers experience around 600€ for a room

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was unfortunately delayed so that our language course registration after the deadline was only possible through kindness of the staff and unfortunately only one online asynchronous Polish course was still available.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
For courses you can register online, however if it is a course outside of the list of electives of the program, you need to ask for approval of the professor and the KJD (make an application on USOS), which can take a while. In my experience it was no problem to take courses outside of the list of electives and you can change courses still in the first 3 weeks of classes.
Language and PE courses can be taken with the use of tokens and in their registration deadlines. Tokens should be in your "account" automatically, but if not, you need to contact your study abroad advisor who will take care of it. For PE courses you have to be fast as soon as the registration period opens, because they fill up fast.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Administrative staff/study abroad advisor

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look through the course catalogue and explore other courses than only the ones indicated by your home university. There are some really interesting courses - you do need them approved by your host university as well though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level felt more like bachelor courses and were rather introductory. Also in some an English language barrier of the teachers was reducing the quality of the classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Generally the majority of courses were more based on lectures and not as interactive as in UCPH. Also, expectations towards the students felt lower as well as the quality of the content.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Communication, Education and Cooperation 4030-CECg
Emerging Sustainable Development Law 4030-ESDLg
Global problems in the contemporary world 4030-GPCW
Human Rights Protection in Europe 4003-PHRE-ERASMUS (Bachelor level)
Measuring, Evaluating and Reporting Sustainability and Innovation 4030-MERSI
Sustainable Development and Beyond. New Concepts for the Future 4030-SDaB
Sustainable Development Economics 4030-SDEg

Non-academic courses:
PE course: Men and women’s volleyball 4023-O-PIŁS3
Polish course: E-learning Polish Course A1 asynchronous online language course (platform based without scheduled video classes) 3004-POLA1-ZAS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Diploma Seminar 4030-DS
MERGED Intra-semester Workshop 4030-MIsW

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Human Rights Protection in Europe 4003-PHRE-ERASMUS: I took this course outside of the electives and learnt a lot about European Human Rights law. The class was more interactive starting with quizzes about the cases that we had to read as preparation for the class and also a mock debate.
Also, if students are interested in sustainability reporting, I suggest the class Measuring, Evaluating and Reporting Sustainability and Innovation [4030-MERSI]. It was one of the more interactive ones and the teachers were very competent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
free sport courses
free language courses
free cultural events
Polish movies for foreigners
the student council also offered regular fun events such as karaoke night
an integration trip at the beginning of the year

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
go to the UCBS integration trip, it is very nice to connect to new people and deepen existing connections with your peers, also to see some Polish countryside and understant a little bit about Polish mindset and life
the sport courses and language courses I would also recommend to get to know polish people and culture and of course language. Polish people highly appreciate when you try to talk and learn Polush!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
museums are often free of charge on different days of the week (see official warsaw website)
go visit Gdansk and Krakow on the weekend, possibly go to zakopane to see the mountains
If you want to go abroad, Berlin is only a 4h trainride
explore the parks in warsaw, especially lazienki

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Fairly easy as people were nice, open and very helpful (even though they might look closed and cold from the outside), however there is a languag barrier than can sometimes make communication hard and some people dont react well to english speaking people.
Also the experience depends on your outer appereance, e.g. skin colour

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
going to the events organised by the student council, sport classes and talk to your polish classmates - i found all of them being super nice and interested in making connections
also try to learn some polish - people really appreciate it even if it is as simple as dzien dobry

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness and kindness of the Polish people, the amazing food and afforable restaraunts and cafes, among many things

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared to be in touch with the administrative office for many things, as the organisation is much more people dependent than in KU, where you can find most things online.
2. try to take courses that are outside of your usual horizon, there are really interesting courses out their
3. try to learn polish and connect with the kind locals

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
OLX has a lot of second hand things to offer
explore the city, go to free museums (I recommend the website
go2warsaw.pl
), go to a free walking tour
connect with polish people

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the people I met: the interesting encounters, perspectives and backgrounds

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: figuring out administrative issues, especially the course registration at the beginning of the year

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
